methodology: Independent ENISA-informed questionnaire; not official ENISA grading.

questions.text: Is someone explicitly accountable for cybersecurity decisions and spend?
questions.explanation: Name a person who owns security decisions and can approve time or budget.
questions.answer_example: Our founder owns security; the IT provider handles changes after approval.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Security decisions have an accountable owner and backup. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Who approves an urgent security fix when the usual owner is away?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Assign a security decision owner and deputy; document their authority and escalation route.
remediation.expected_outcome: Security decisions have an accountable owner and backup.
remediation.verification: Named owner/deputy and an approved responsibility note.

questions.text: Are all staff and contractors taught practical phishing/account-security basics at onboarding?
questions.explanation: Include employees and contractors. Look for practical onboarding, not just a policy link.
questions.answer_example: New starters get phishing examples and an MFA walkthrough; contractors are not yet included.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Every new starter receives practical security instruction. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: When was the latest starter trained, and where is completion recorded?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Add practical phishing, MFA and reporting guidance to onboarding for staff and contractors; track completion.
remediation.expected_outcome: Every new starter receives practical security instruction.
remediation.verification: Onboarding checklist and anonymized completion records.

questions.text: Can staff report suspicious messages or incidents quickly without guessing whom to contact?
questions.explanation: People should know a clear, quick way to report suspicious activity.
questions.answer_example: We use a dedicated email and chat channel monitored by the operations lead.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Staff can report suspicious activity and receive a response. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Who monitors reports outside normal working hours?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Publish one reporting channel and a monitored escalation contact; test a suspicious-message report.
remediation.expected_outcome: Staff can report suspicious activity and receive a response.
remediation.verification: Published instructions and a test report with response time.

questions.text: Do owners of privileged/financial accounts know how to recognize and challenge suspicious requests?
questions.explanation: Check whether people handling money or admin access independently verify unusual requests.
questions.answer_example: Bank-detail changes require a callback to a known number and a second approver.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Impersonation requests face an independent verification step. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How would you verify an urgent payment request apparently from the founder?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Require independent verification of payment, bank-detail and privileged-access requests using known contact details.
remediation.expected_outcome: Impersonation requests face an independent verification step.
remediation.verification: Approved procedure and a redacted example of dual approval.

questions.text: Are contractor access rights reviewed when their work changes or ends?
questions.explanation: Remove or adjust contractor access when roles or engagements change.
questions.answer_example: The project owner checks accounts at contract end; SaaS access is still manual.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Expired contractor access is removed consistently. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Which accounts did the most recent departing contractor lose access to?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Track contractor accounts and review access at role changes and contract end.
remediation.expected_outcome: Expired contractor access is removed consistently.
remediation.verification: Redacted access review and one completed offboarding record.

questions.text: Are security responsibilities documented for outsourced IT or SaaS providers?
questions.explanation: Write down what your provider secures, what you secure, and how issues are escalated.
questions.answer_example: Our IT agreement lists patching and backup responsibilities but not incident reporting.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Provider and internal responsibilities are unambiguous. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Who is responsible if the provider detects an account compromise?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Document security responsibilities, incident notification and escalation with each critical IT provider.
remediation.expected_outcome: Provider and internal responsibilities are unambiguous.
remediation.verification: Responsibility matrix and agreed escalation/notification terms.

questions.text: Is security discussed with company leadership when changes or purchases are proposed?
questions.explanation: Include security in leadership decisions about products, vendors and spending.
questions.answer_example: Leadership reviews major risks monthly and assigns a named owner for decisions.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Leadership explicitly funds or accepts material security risks. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: What was the most recent security decision leadership made?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Add a short security-risk review to leadership decisions about products, vendors and material changes.
remediation.expected_outcome: Leadership explicitly funds or accepts material security risks.
remediation.verification: Decision log with a risk, owner and recorded decision.

questions.text: Do teams practice an incident scenario (e.g., account compromise) at least annually?
questions.explanation: Rehearse a realistic incident so people know their roles before an emergency.
questions.answer_example: We rehearsed a stolen admin account scenario and logged actions to improve.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: The team can rehearse and improve incident decisions. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Which improvement from the latest exercise has been completed?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Run an account-compromise tabletop exercise, record gaps and assign improvement owners and dates.
dependencies: Incident contacts and basic response plan
remediation.expected_outcome: The team can rehearse and improve incident decisions.
remediation.verification: Exercise record and tracked follow-up actions.

questions.text: Do staff understand rules for handling customer, financial and proprietary data?
questions.explanation: People should know which data is sensitive and how to share, store and dispose of it.
questions.answer_example: Staff use approved storage and avoid customer data in personal chat or AI tools.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Staff understand where sensitive data may be stored and shared. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How are staff told which data can be shared with external tools?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Publish simple handling rules for customer, financial and proprietary data, including external sharing and AI tools.
remediation.expected_outcome: Staff understand where sensitive data may be stored and shared.
remediation.verification: Handling guidance and an anonymized awareness check.

questions.text: Is security training adjusted after incidents, process changes, or identified weaknesses?
questions.explanation: Use incidents and observed weaknesses to improve training, then check understanding.
questions.answer_example: After a phishing report, we updated onboarding and tested the new reporting steps.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Training responds to actual weaknesses. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How did you check whether the change improved staff behavior?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Review incidents and observed training gaps; update guidance and check whether staff apply the changes.
remediation.expected_outcome: Training responds to actual weaknesses.
remediation.verification: Updated material, reason for change and follow-up check.

questions.text: Is there an up-to-date list of critical business services, systems and data owners?
questions.explanation: List services that matter to the business, their systems, data and accountable owners.
questions.answer_example: A shared inventory maps our app, identity provider and customer database to owners.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Critical services and dependencies are visible. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: When was the inventory last reviewed and who updates it?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Inventory critical business services, supporting systems, important data and accountable owners.
remediation.expected_outcome: Critical services and dependencies are visible.
remediation.verification: Dated inventory reviewed by service owners.

questions.text: Is there a recurring process for ranking cyber risks by business impact and likelihood?
questions.explanation: Rank specific risks using business impact and likelihood, and revisit them regularly.
questions.answer_example: We review a risk register each quarter; customer-data loss and account takeover rank highest.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Security work follows documented business priorities. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: What changed since the last risk review, and did priorities change?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Create a small risk register with impact, likelihood, owner, treatment and review date; review it regularly.
remediation.expected_outcome: Security work follows documented business priorities.
remediation.verification: Reviewed register with treatment decisions and owners.

questions.text: Are key legal, privacy, contractual and customer security obligations tracked?
questions.explanation: Track security and privacy obligations from contracts and applicable requirements.
questions.answer_example: Customer contracts and privacy obligations are tracked with owners and review dates.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Security commitments are discoverable and assigned. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Who checks a new customer contract for security commitments?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Track contractual, privacy and applicable security obligations with accountable owners and review dates.
remediation.expected_outcome: Security commitments are discoverable and assigned.
remediation.verification: Obligations register referencing source requirements.

questions.text: Is there a documented incident response contact list and initial containment process?
questions.explanation: Keep usable incident contacts and initial steps for containing likely incidents.
questions.answer_example: Our runbook lists the incident lead, provider contacts and account lockout steps.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: The team can contact the right people and contain common incidents. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Could the team access the runbook if company email were unavailable?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Write and rehearse initial steps for account compromise and service disruption; keep offline-accessible contacts.
dependencies: Named response owner and provider contacts
remediation.expected_outcome: The team can contact the right people and contain common incidents.
remediation.verification: Accessible runbook and a dated contact/response exercise.

questions.text: Are access requests/approvals and offboarding consistently documented?
questions.explanation: Document access approvals and reliably remove access when people leave.
questions.answer_example: The manager approves access by ticket; offboarding includes identity, Git and SaaS accounts.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Access is approved and promptly removed when no longer needed. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How was the latest offboarding checked for missed accounts?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Use a documented approval and offboarding checklist covering identity, cloud, code and SaaS access.
remediation.expected_outcome: Access is approved and promptly removed when no longer needed.
remediation.verification: Approved access request and completed offboarding sample.

questions.text: Is there a backup and recovery plan with defined recovery needs for critical services?
questions.explanation: Define which services need recovery, how quickly, and how much data loss is tolerable.
questions.answer_example: The app must recover within a day with no more than a day's data loss; the plan names an owner.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Recovery priorities match business needs. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Have recovery targets been tested against a real restore?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Set recovery-time and data-loss targets for critical services; document backup owners and restore dependencies.
remediation.expected_outcome: Recovery priorities match business needs.
remediation.verification: Approved recovery targets and a recovery runbook.

questions.text: Are material cloud/SaaS vendors evaluated and reassessed for security dependencies?
questions.explanation: Check critical vendors before use and when their access or risk changes.
questions.answer_example: We review security information and data access for critical vendors annually.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Material vendor risks are reviewed before and during use. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Which vendor failure would cause the biggest business interruption?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Assess critical vendors for data access, service dependency and incident handling; schedule reassessment.
remediation.expected_outcome: Material vendor risks are reviewed before and during use.
remediation.verification: Completed review with findings, owner and next review date.

questions.text: Is there a routine to patch, remediate, or accept risks with named owners and deadlines?
questions.explanation: Give findings an owner and due date; record risk acceptance rather than silently ignoring them.
questions.answer_example: We track patches and vulnerabilities with deadlines; exceptions need founder approval.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Findings are fixed or explicitly accepted within agreed deadlines. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: What happens when a high-priority finding passes its deadline?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Track remediation findings with owners and deadlines; document exceptions and escalate overdue high risks.
remediation.expected_outcome: Findings are fixed or explicitly accepted within agreed deadlines.
remediation.verification: Remediation backlog and an approved exception example.

questions.text: Are security-impacting changes reviewed, tested and logged before release?
questions.explanation: Review and test security-impacting changes before deploying them and retain a record.
questions.answer_example: Cloud permissions and production changes require review and a rollback plan.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Important changes are traceable and recoverable. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How could you trace the last production permission change?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Require review, testing and a rollback plan for security-impacting production and permission changes.
remediation.expected_outcome: Important changes are traceable and recoverable.
remediation.verification: Reviewed change record with test and rollback evidence.

questions.text: Are recovery and incident response plans tested, and lessons incorporated into improvements?
questions.explanation: Test recovery and incident plans, record lessons, and follow through on improvements.
questions.answer_example: A recovery exercise found a missing secret; the runbook and recovery process were corrected.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Plans work in practice and improve after testing. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Who verifies that exercise actions are closed?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Test an actual recovery and incident scenario; record lessons and verify improvement actions are closed.
remediation.expected_outcome: Plans work in practice and improve after testing.
remediation.verification: Exercise/restore report and closed improvement tickets.

questions.text: Is phishing-resistant MFA enabled on privileged accounts and MFA on other critical accounts wherever supported?
questions.explanation: Prioritize admin, email and financial accounts. Passkeys or security keys resist phishing where supported.
questions.answer_example: Admin accounts use security keys; other critical accounts use MFA; one vendor is an exception.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Critical accounts have effective MFA with owned exceptions. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Which critical accounts are still exceptions, and who owns fixing them?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Inventory critical accounts, enable phishing-resistant MFA for admins where supported, and track remaining MFA exceptions.
dependencies: Critical account list and recovery-access plan
remediation.expected_outcome: Critical accounts have effective MFA with owned exceptions.
remediation.verification: Redacted MFA coverage report and exception register.

questions.text: Are endpoints and operating systems supported, protected and updated?
questions.explanation: Use supported operating systems, apply updates and check protection is functioning.
questions.answer_example: Company laptops are supported, centrally updated and monitored for protection failures.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Endpoints stay supported, updated and protected. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How do you find devices that missed updates or lost protection?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Inventory endpoints, replace unsupported systems and establish a monitored update/protection routine.
remediation.expected_outcome: Endpoints stay supported, updated and protected.
remediation.verification: Patch/support status report and protection-health review.

questions.text: Are essential data and settings backed up, with restore tests completed?
questions.explanation: A backup is only useful if you can restore it. Include essential settings and dependencies.
questions.answer_example: Daily backups are separate from production; a sample restore was tested last month.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Backups can restore essential service data within agreed needs. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: What was restored, how long did it take, and did you verify its integrity?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Back up essential data and configuration separately from production; test a representative restore and measure recovery.
remediation.expected_outcome: Backups can restore essential service data within agreed needs.
remediation.verification: Restore test recording integrity checks, duration and gaps.

questions.text: Are admin privileges minimized and accounts uniquely attributable to individuals?
questions.explanation: Use individual accounts and only the permissions people actually need.
questions.answer_example: Staff have unique accounts; admin access is limited and reviewed quarterly.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Privileged actions are attributable and access is limited. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Which users currently have privileged access, and why?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Replace shared identities with individual accounts; remove unnecessary admin access and review privileges regularly.
remediation.expected_outcome: Privileged actions are attributable and access is limited.
remediation.verification: Privileged-access review and removal/approval records.

questions.text: Is there a maintained inventory of cloud, SaaS, devices and critical external services?
questions.explanation: Track cloud accounts, SaaS, devices and external services, including their owners.
questions.answer_example: Our inventory includes approved SaaS and devices, but personal subscriptions need review.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Important assets and shadow services are visible. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How would you discover a tool bought outside the normal approval process?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Maintain a cloud, SaaS, device and external-service inventory with owners; check for unapproved tools.
remediation.expected_outcome: Important assets and shadow services are visible.
remediation.verification: Dated asset list and reconciliation/review results.

questions.text: Are sensitive data encrypted in transit and at rest where applicable?
questions.explanation: Check how sensitive data is protected while moving and while stored, including backups.
questions.answer_example: Customer traffic uses TLS; databases and backups are encrypted with managed keys.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Sensitive data is encrypted with controlled key access. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Who can access encryption keys or decrypt sensitive data?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Check encryption for sensitive data flows, storage and backups; review key access and remediate gaps.
remediation.expected_outcome: Sensitive data is encrypted with controlled key access.
remediation.verification: Redacted configuration review and key-access inventory.

questions.text: Are critical cloud/SaaS configurations reviewed against secure defaults?
questions.explanation: Review critical configurations rather than assuming vendor defaults are always sufficient.
questions.answer_example: We check cloud storage, sharing and identity settings against a documented baseline.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Critical services follow reviewed secure configurations. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: When did the last configuration review occur and what changed?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Review critical cloud/SaaS sharing, storage and identity settings against a documented secure baseline.
remediation.expected_outcome: Critical services follow reviewed secure configurations.
remediation.verification: Baseline comparison and remediation/exception records.

questions.text: Do critical systems produce accessible security logs and actionable alerts?
questions.explanation: Collect useful logs and assign someone to act on meaningful security alerts.
questions.answer_example: Admin sign-ins and cloud changes are logged; suspicious login alerts go to the on-call owner.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Important suspicious events are visible and assigned for action. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: How do you know alerts are reaching someone and being acted on?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Enable useful security logs and route actionable alerts to a named responder; test delivery and response.
remediation.expected_outcome: Important suspicious events are visible and assigned for action.
remediation.verification: Logging coverage, retention settings and an alert-response test.

questions.text: Are publicly exposed systems/dependencies scanned and findings prioritized and remediated?
questions.explanation: Find exposed systems and vulnerable dependencies, then remediate according to risk.
questions.answer_example: Our pipeline checks dependencies weekly; internet-facing findings get assigned deadlines.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Exposed vulnerabilities are found and treated according to risk. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: Which unresolved public-facing finding has the highest business impact?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Scan internet-facing systems and software dependencies; prioritize findings by exposure and track remediation.
remediation.expected_outcome: Exposed vulnerabilities are found and treated according to risk.
remediation.verification: Recent scan report and linked remediation/exception records.

questions.text: Are secrets kept in managed stores rather than source code, personal chats or shared documents?
questions.explanation: Use managed secret stores and rotate exposed secrets; avoid code, chat and shared files.
questions.answer_example: Production credentials are in a secret manager with scoped access and rotation procedures.

follow_ups.low: What is missing to achieve this outcome: Production secrets are controlled and exposed credentials can be rotated. Who will address it?
follow_ups.high: What happens if a developer accidentally commits a secret?
follow_ups.unknown: Who can check this control, and which evidence would resolve whether it is in place?
follow_ups.na: Which part of your business makes this control inapplicable, and when should that decision be reviewed?

remediation.action: Move secrets into a managed store, scope access and define rotation and accidental-exposure response.
remediation.expected_outcome: Production secrets are controlled and exposed credentials can be rotated.
remediation.verification: Secret-storage/access review and a rotation exercise record.
